elementary_first_supplier: A compact properly embedded surface in a ball whose every component has boundary has a geometric compressing disk whenever a component is not a disk. Cap a curve parallel to that component boundary using the boundary sphere; minimize interior circle intersections with the surface. Inessential intersections admit innermost surface-disk surgery of the auxiliary disk; an essential innermost circle gives the compression. If no interior circles remain, the original auxiliary disk is a compression.
decomposing_sphere_application: A compression curve on the two-punctured sphere cannot separate the two punctures: capping either punctured side would produce a sphere meeting the closed link once. It therefore bounds a puncture-free surface disk. Compression-disk replacement removes that disk and yields an isotopic decomposing sphere through a link-free ball, by nonsplitting and Schoenflies. This removes cut curves and whole saddles rather than creating them.
